title: The Indus Valley civilisation
examples: What makes the Indus Valley Civilization so important?
How did they manage the waste in their cities?
Were Harappa and Mohenjo-daro the only big cities?

explain.say: Today we explore the Indus Valley Civilization. We will look at two main sites. These were Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.
These two sites show us amazing things about ancient life. They were major centers of trade and culture.
The people built very well planned cities. Streets were laid out in neat grids. This shows careful planning.
A key feature was their advanced drainage system. Every house connected to main drains. This kept the cities clean.
In real life, modern cities still use these ideas. We still need good drainage for rain. This keeps our streets from flooding.
A common mistake is thinking they used simple ditches. They actually had covered drains under the streets. This was much more sophisticated.

faq.q: Why are Harappa and Mohenjo-daro so important to history?
faq.a: They are important because they show evidence of highly organized urban life. They prove that complex societies existed in the Bronze Age.
asks: What do these sites tell us?

faq.q: Were all their cities built the same way?
faq.a: No, while they shared planning ideas, some areas might have developed differently. The core principles of grid planning remained consistent.
They used sophisticated covered drainage systems connected to every dwelling. This was a major achievement in early urban planning.
asks: What was their waste removal system?

faq.q: Did they have writing that we can read?
faq.a: They had a script, but we have not yet fully deciphered what it means. It remains a mystery to archaeologists.

faq.q: Were they the only advanced civilization?
faq.a: No, other civilizations developed great things too. However, the planning at Mohenjo-daro is remarkable for its time.
asks: Were they the first advanced people?
How did they compare to others?

facts: The civilization flourished around the Indus River Valley.
Cities were laid out using a precise grid pattern of main streets.
Sophisticated drainage systems were covered and connected to homes.
Major sites include Harappa and Mohenjo-daro.

quiz.why: A grid pattern shows that people thought about the city's structure before building.

wrong.0: The grid shows multiple intersecting roads, not just one path.
wrong.1: The scale of the grid indicates a large, complex settlement.
wrong.3: This suggests people just built where they found space, not with a plan.

quiz.say: The presence of covered drains indicates:

options.show: They did not have private toilets.
options.say: They did not have private toilets.

quiz.why: Having covered drains shows they understood waste management was important for health.

wrong.0: The drain system implies waste was managed from within homes.
wrong.1: The drain system was specifically designed to keep the city clean.
wrong.3: This ignores the evidence of complex plumbing systems under the streets.

quiz.say: If a city had drains connecting every house, it means:

options.show: Only the main street was cleaned.
options.say: Only the main street was cleaned.

options.show: They used rivers for all waste.
options.say: They used rivers for all waste.

quiz.why: This shows that the drainage was a community-wide system, not just for one area.

wrong.0: The existence of the system proves they solved the problem successfully.
wrong.2: The evidence shows connections from individual dwellings to the drains.
wrong.3: While rivers were used, the primary system was engineered drainage.
